title: Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa (Venice) to the Catholic Monarchs, 24 Feb 1504: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 93, f. 118r-v, key not identified (catalogue item 9)

documents.route: Lorenzo Suárez de Figueroa, Venice -> the Catholic Monarchs

transcription.source: f. 118r lines 1-21 sign by sign; segmentation of the page gives 910 glyphs on 33 lines (targets/esp318/f118r_glyphs.pkl)
transcription.notes: Transcribed as a character stream in which the CVC code groups are split into letter signs; covers lines 1-21 of f. 118r only.

system.summary: A cipher of Ferdinand's secretariat: single invented signs for letters, with homophones, interleaved with groups of two to four Latin letters (nomenclator); the groups are atomic code units.
system.sibling_key: unknown; Escrivà no. 1 and the Cifra general excluded by code initials; no. 94's key (recovered by Brackx 2026, esp318no94) does not fit; the Gran cifra of 1501-04 (Bergenroth's partial reconstruction, BNE MSS 20.211/52) not obtained
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from esp318 (the whole volume) under the one-key rule; held nos. 93 and 94 until 21 Oct 2026, when no. 94 (key recovered by Michael Brackx, issue #62) moved to its own entry esp318no94: the code inventories barely overlap (no. 93's gto, pie, heg, zoe, zoc, hug never occur in no. 94). Other entries: esp318 (no. 92), federico1497 (no. 5), esp318no94 (no. 94), esp318no95 (no. 95).

prior_solution.where: No decipherment in the volume or in print (Parisi, Galende Díaz, Tomokiyo, Quirantes)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: seg.py, glyphs.py, cluster.py (segmentation of f. 118r; in targets/esp318/)
solve93.py (homophonic annealing against a Spanish 5-gram model)

solution.what: Mapped the five ciphered letters in the volume from the manifest and notice; nos. 93 (f. 118r-v) and 94 (ff. 120r-121v) have no decipherment anywhere in the volume.

No. 93 f. 118r segmented and clustered: sign alphabet plus CVC groups; the code initials of both letters fall outside the two keys in print (Escrivà no. 1, Cifra general) and inside the band of the Gran cifra.

No. 93 as plain homophonic letter stream (ct93_eye.txt, 1016 tokens), annealed against Spanish 5-grams from eight starts: best -3.5 nats/token against -1.8 for real Spanish; the CVC groups are atomic.

Split from the former whole-volume target esp318 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): nos. 93 and 94 kept together as one attempted entry with no shared-key claim. ct93_eye.txt and solve93.py moved here.

Michael Brackx (issue #62) recovered no. 94's alphabet and reported that it does not break no. 93 (no convergence, best -3.08 nats/char; fixing the shared glyphs to no. 94's values makes it worse; 7 shared groups). Checked here on the code inventories: no. 93's top trigrams (gto x21, pie x19, heg x13, zoe, zoc, hug) never occur in no. 94; no. 94's qa, rah, mny, qag absent from ct93_eye.txt except pif x2; muy x3 in no. 93. No. 94 split into esp318no94.

outcome.method_basis: No key for no. 93: the two keys in print are excluded by code-initial range, no. 94's key (Brackx 2026) does not fit, the suspected Gran cifra survives only as Bergenroth's partial list in a manuscript not served online, and a homophonic anneal of no. 93 as a letter stream failed.

gaps.detail: CVC nomenclator with atomic groups (homophonic anneal on ct93_eye.txt failed, -3.5 vs -1.8 nats); the suspected Gran cifra key survives only as Bergenroth's partial list (BNE MSS 20.211/52); no. 94's key (Brackx 2026) does not fit it

outcome.notes: Attempted, open. No. 94 split off on 21 Oct 2026 (esp318no94).

credits.note: showed no. 94 is in a different key from no. 93 (no convergence with no. 94's alphabet, 7 shared code groups, different initials); the entry was split
